sessions.title: Choose the admitted form of one or two

steps.title: Choose one by gender
steps.body: один мальчик — one boy; одна девушка — one girl. For these singular counting examples, one agrees with the noun: masculine один and feminine одна. Both still mean one. Guided practice uses мальчик.

steps.title: Choose the form of two
steps.body: два is the form for masculine and neuter counted nouns; две is the feminine form. The supplied example две девушки — two girls uses feminine две. The following noun is genitive singular in this counting construction; the numeral choice still follows its gender.

steps.title: Recognize neuter and plural-form one
steps.body: одно животное — one animal uses neuter singular одно. одни джинсы — one [pair of] jeans uses plural одни with the plural-form noun. The plural numeral here does not mean several pairs; these are different gender/number forms of one.

steps.title: Keep the value while changing agreement
steps.body: одна́ and одно́ both represent 1 in the retained cardinal table. They are feminine and neuter singular forms, respectively. The existing table stress is retained; the separate counting examples are printed without added stress.

steps.title: Distinguish plural one from feminine two
steps.body: одни́ represents 1 in the supplied plural-form example, while две represents 2 with a feminine noun. Distinguish одни джинсы from две девушки by the complete supplied construction, rather than treating every plural-looking form as two.

steps.title: Apply masculine one to a different noun
steps.body: оди́н — one and два — two retain their supplied values. The additional source example один час supplies masculine singular один with час. The independent masculine check uses this different noun from guided мальчик. Choose один rather than feminine одна for час in this counting context; this is supplied-form recognition, not all numeral cases or unrestricted sentence production.

steps.title: Guided practice

steps.title: Independent checks
steps.body: Choose the supplied form of one or two for the noun and counting context. A missed check returns to the complete explanation.

steps.title: Start with the construction
steps.body: These basic counting examples use nominative phrases. The related noun-case pattern also applies in inanimate accusative contexts, with the appropriate noun form. Other sentence cases require numeral declension as well as noun declension. A count ending in one outside the teen exception uses a nominative singular noun in the shown basic phrases. один час — один час. два часа — два часа.

steps.title: Two, three and four
steps.body: A count ending in two, three or four outside the teen exception uses a genitive singular noun in the basic construction. This is a grammatical singular form even though the count is greater than one.

steps.title: Genitive plural counts
steps.body: Counts ending in zero or five through nine use genitive plural in the basic construction. The teen exception also uses genitive plural. Ten and sixteen therefore fit this pattern. пять часов — пять часов. двадцать один час — двадцать один час.

steps.title: Compound counts
steps.body: For a compound count, inspect the last two digits first. If they are 11, 12, 13 or 14, use genitive plural for the counted noun in the basic construction. Otherwise, the final digit selects the pattern: one, two-through-four, or zero/five-through-nine. Compare 21 and 22: their final digits select different noun cases; being larger than five is not enough to choose genitive plural. двадцать два часа — двадцать два часа. две девушки — two girls.

steps.title: Teen values and exceptions
steps.body: For a compound count, inspect the last two digits first. If they are 11, 12, 13 or 14, use genitive plural for the counted noun in the basic construction. Otherwise, the final digit selects the pattern: one, two-through-four, or zero/five-through-nine. All counts from 11 through19 use genitive plural here. For 15 through19 the final digit already leads to genitive plural;11 through14 override the one/two/three/four ending pattern. пять девушек — five girls. шестнадцать рублей — sixteen rubles.

steps.title: One and zero endings
steps.body: The example with 41 follows the final-one pattern and uses nominative singular for the counted noun. The example with 10 follows the zero-ending pattern and uses genitive plural. десять копеек — ten kopeks. сорок один год — forty-one years.

steps.title: Hundreds preserve the boundary
steps.body: The count 203 ends in 03, so final three selects genitive singular in the basic counting phrase. The count 213 ends in 13, so the teen exception selects genitive plural. пять лет — пять лет. двести три собаки — two hundred and three dogs.

steps.title: Compare the supplied hundreds
steps.body: For a compound count, inspect the last two digits first. If they are 11, 12, 13 or 14, use genitive plural for the counted noun in the basic construction. Otherwise, the final digit selects the pattern: one, two-through-four, or zero/five-through-nine. Compare the supplied 203 and 213 examples and the two kopeck examples. Count value and sentence construction govern the explanation. двести тринадцать собак — two hundred and thirteen dogs. Два́дцать две копе́йки — 22 kopecks.

steps.title: A sentence outside the basic pattern
steps.body: The I saw two friends sentence has an animate accusative object. Both the numeral and noun are declined; do not classify it with the basic nominative/inanimate accusative rule. The one-cat example below instead states existence in the basic nominative context. Я видел двух друзей — I saw two friends. Есть оди́н кот — There is one cat.
